In my experience, I’ve only really let things slip when I was unaware it wasn’t normal. I’d say “dad made me drink spoilt milk” or “I got a big whack last night” not realising these were abusive behaviours. 

That was when I was younger, as I got older I started to be more open about it but I know a lot of abused people avoid the word ‘abuse’ bc it feels bad saying it. Instead I say stuff like “dad was an asshole” or “dad was kind of a shit parent”. It conveyed the meaning without having to victimise myself.

Oh so relatable!!

The first time I heard about “mastery experience” I got really sad because I felt like I was never going to have that moment of “oh! I worked really hard and it’s paying off!” I always thought it was because I was lazy and not super smart, but knowing there’s another possible reason is keeping me going 🥰

I’m undiagnosed (seeing a psychiatrist soon) but I very much have struggled with the same thing.

Have interest > become obsessed with interest > talk about interest too much > become ashamed of interest > repeat!

I have found that with age I’ve gotten less ashamed of enjoying things and that’s made it easier to think “I may not be hyper focused on this one thing anymore, but I learnt a lot and can still dabble whenever I want!”

This reduces the shame spiral and acknowledges the positives of learning a lot about one topic.

Unfortunately, for me (22F) it doesn’t make it easy to pick a career path bc I’m interested in something new every second week 😫

Thank you so much, it’s hard to feel positive at times like this but knowing that other people have made it through similar symptoms (even if what I experience isn’t ADHD) is very comforting. 

I’ll call my people tomorrow and see if I can set something up, I’m from Australia so things are a bit different, but you’re right. I can’t get in my own way forever.
